sources.section: Package indexes > Pinning a package to an index
Package indexes > Searching across multiple indexes

tasks.answer: Define the private index as a named `[[tool.uv.index]]` and pin the package to it with `[tool.uv.sources]` `pkg = { index = "<name>" }` (optionally `explicit = true` so the index serves only pinned packages); with the default `first-index` strategy a package found on that index is never taken from PyPI.

sources.section: Caching > Cache directory
Caching > Clearing the cache

tasks.answer: Set `UV_CACHE_DIR` (or `--cache-dir` / `tool.uv.cache-dir`) to move the cache, and run `uv cache prune` to remove only unused cache entries (unlike `uv cache clean`, which removes everything).

sources.section: Using uv in GitHub Actions > Caching
Caching > Caching in continuous integration

tasks.answer: Use `astral-sh/setup-uv` with `enable-cache: true`, or manage it with `actions/cache` on a constant `UV_CACHE_DIR` keyed on `hashFiles('uv.lock')`, and run `uv cache prune --ci` at the end of the job.

sources.section: Running scripts > Declaring script dependencies

tasks.answer: Run `uv add --script example.py <deps>` to write an inline `# /// script` metadata block with `dependencies = [...]` (and optionally `requires-python`), then `uv run example.py` builds an environment with those dependencies.

sources.section: Using uv with PyTorch > Using a PyTorch index
Using uv with PyTorch > Installing PyTorch

tasks.answer: Add a `[[tool.uv.index]]` for the CUDA wheel index (e.g. `name = "pytorch-cu130"`, `url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130"`, `explicit = true`) and point `torch`/`torchvision` at it in `[tool.uv.sources]`, gated with a `sys_platform` marker for Linux/Windows.

sources.section: Tools > The `uv tool` interface
Tools > Execution vs installation
Tools > Tool environments

tasks.answer: `uvx` (an alias of `uv tool run`) runs a tool in a temporary, disposable environment kept in the uv cache, while `uv tool install` creates a persistent environment in the tools directory and puts the tool's executables on the `PATH` until it is uninstalled.

sources.section: Locking and syncing > Automatic lock and sync
Locking and syncing > Checking the lockfile

tasks.answer: Pass `--locked` (e.g. `uv sync --locked`), which raises an error instead of updating an out-of-date lockfile, or run `uv lock --check`.

sources.section: Using workspaces > Workspace sources
Managing dependencies > Dependency sources > Workspace member

tasks.answer: List the member in `project.dependencies` and add it to `[tool.uv.sources]` with `{ workspace = true }` (e.g. `bird-feeder = { workspace = true }`); such dependencies are editable.

sources.section: TLS certificates > System certificates

tasks.answer: Pass `--system-certs`, set `UV_SYSTEM_CERTS=true`, or set `system-certs = true` in `uv.toml` so uv uses the platform's native certificate store instead of its bundled Mozilla roots.

sources.section: Building distributions > Preventing publish to PyPI

tasks.answer: Add the classifier `"Private :: Do Not Upload"` to `[project] classifiers`, which makes PyPI reject the upload (and use per-project PyPI API tokens).

sources.section: Exporting a lockfile > Overview of export formats
Exporting a lockfile > `requirements.txt` format > Basic usage

tasks.answer: Run `uv export --format requirements.txt --output-file requirements.txt` (without `--output-file` it prints to stdout).

sources.section: AWS CodeArtifact > Authenticate with an AWS access token
AWS CodeArtifact > Authenticate with `keyring` and `keyrings.codeartifact`

tasks.answer: Generate a token with `aws codeartifact get-authorization-token` and set `UV_INDEX_<NAME>_USERNAME=aws` and `UV_INDEX_<NAME>_PASSWORD` to it for the named index (or use `keyring` with `keyrings.codeartifact` and `UV_KEYRING_PROVIDER=subprocess`).

sources.section: Using uv in Docker > Optimizations > Intermediate layers
Using uv in Docker > Optimizations > Caching

tasks.answer: First run `uv sync --frozen --no-install-project` with only `uv.lock` bind-mounted (and a cache mount on `/root/.cache/uv`), then `COPY` the project and run `uv sync --locked`, so the dependency layer is reused while the project changes.

sources.section: Configuring projects > Conflicting dependencies
Resolution > Conflicting dependencies

tasks.answer: Declare them under `[tool.uv]` as `conflicts = [[{ extra = "extra1" }, { extra = "extra2" }]]`, so uv resolves them separately (and refuses to install both together).

sources.section: Preview features > Enabling preview features

tasks.answer: Use `--preview-features <name>` (or `UV_PREVIEW_FEATURES`, or `preview-features = ["<name>"]` in `uv.toml`/`[tool.uv]`) for a specific feature, or `--preview` / `UV_PREVIEW=1` for all of them.

sources.section: Python versions > Requesting a version > Python version files
Python versions > Project Python versions

tasks.answer: Run `uv python pin <version>`, which writes a `.python-version` file that uv uses as the default request (within the project's `requires-python`).
